findings.issue_text: GroupTest.java:157 checks caughtExceptions without first joining the reader thread, allowing an in-flight read to record an exception after the assertion passes and causing the regression test to miss the failure.

GroupTest.java:152 skips deletedAll.set(true) if group deletion throws, leaving the reader thread issuing requests indefinitely, including during subsequent tests; the reader must be stopped and joined in a finally block.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupTest.java:152 skips deletedAll.set(true) if group deletion throws, leaving the reader thread issuing requests indefinitely, including during subsequent tests; the reader must be stopped and joined in a finally block.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that if any group deletion throws an exception, the loop will exit without setting deletedAll.set(true), causing the reader thread to continue running indefinitely with its while (!deletedAll.get()) loop. This is a real test code defect - the deletedAll.set(true) should be in a finally block to ensure the reader thread terminates regardless of exceptions during deletion. The reader thread would continue making requests during subsequent tests, potentially causing test interference.
